tips.text: The UK FCDO describes road surfaces as poor, especially in rural areas, with unmarked roadworks, potholes and unlit vehicles at night, and Canada warns that driving conditions may be hazardous in winter, particularly on mountain roads in northern and southeastern Albania.

If you hold a valid multiple-entry Schengen, EU, UK or US visa that you have already used (or a residence permit from those countries), you can enter Albania visa-free even if your passport normally requires a visa. Iranian citizens are excluded.
Carry lek in cash: the Government of Canada says cash is needed for small purchases and in rural areas, while credit cards are accepted in major cities.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Albania?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and dozens of other countries enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. If your passport does need a visa, you can apply online at e-visa.al or at an Albanian embassy, or enter visa-free if you hold a valid, already-used multiple-entry Schengen, EU, UK or US visa.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Albania?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how long US citizens may stay. The Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs' visa-regime table lists them as visa-free.

faq.question: Can I enter Albania with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes, for most nationalities. A valid multiple-entry Schengen, EU, UK or US visa that you have already used in the country that issued it (or a Schengen, EU, UK or US residence permit) lets otherwise visa-required nationalities enter Albania visa-free; leave at least 3 days before it expires. Single-entry Schengen visas do not qualify, and the exemption does not apply to Iranian citizens.

faq.question: Is Albania in the Schengen Area or the EU?
faq.answer: No — Albania belongs to neither the EU nor the Schengen Area.

faq.question: What currency is used in Albania, and can I pay in euros?
faq.answer: The Albanian lek (ALL). The Government of Canada says credit cards are accepted in major cities but cash is needed for small purchases and in rural areas. No official source we could read describes paying in euros.
